selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does this passage mostly teach about Allah and the world?
questions.answer: Allah alone made and runs everything.

questions.question: Why are so many titles used for Allah here?
questions.answer: To show He is in charge of everything in every way.

questions.question: What did the traveler notice in the whole universe?
questions.answer: Very fine order and regularity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah needing a minister or aide?
questions.answer: He does not need any.

questions.question: What can we understand when the same kinds of elements are found across the earth?
questions.answer: One Lord spread them and governs them.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah and helpers?
questions.answer: He does not need helpers.

questions.question: What is special about many things in the world even though they are in many places?
questions.answer: They are alike in kind and follow the same plan.

questions.question: What is the meaning of saying Allah has no opposite?
questions.answer: Nothing can stand against Him as a rival.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah and partners?
questions.answer: Allah has no partners.

questions.question: What faith lesson should a Muslim child take from this passage?
questions.answer: We should believe Allah alone made, owns, and manages everything.

questions.question: Who is called the Maker, Disposer, Monarch, Nurturer, Master, and Builder in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: Who noticed this truth at that stage?
questions.answer: The traveler.

questions.question: The passage compares the world to a palace. What does that comparison help us understand?
questions.answer: The world is arranged on purpose, not by accident.

questions.question: What does it mean that many things follow a general scheme?
questions.answer: They fit into one big plan.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a city and a palace?
questions.answer: To help us picture a place that is ruled and arranged.

questions.question: The passage talks about the whole cosmos, its parts, and the beings in it. What do they all help prove?
questions.answer: They help prove Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is the meaning of saying Allah has no equal?
questions.answer: No one is like Him.

questions.question: What can a student infer when one style of care is seen in the whole world?
questions.answer: The same Creator is caring for all of it.

questions.question: What can we learn about Allah’s power from this passage?
questions.answer: His power reaches the whole universe.

questions.question: How does this passage help someone answer, “Who runs the world?”
questions.answer: Allah alone runs it.

questions.question: What stage is mentioned at the start of this truth?
questions.answer: The second stage.

questions.question: What does “regularity” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: Things happen in a steady, organized way.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the cosmos, its pillars, its parts, and its beings?
questions.answer: To show the proof is everywhere.

questions.question: What does that teach us about Allah’s care?
questions.answer: His care covers all things.
